analyst_view.overall: Early view: Burgos, third, are strong at El Plantío and Sergio Francisco wants control rather than an open game, though Jon Karrikaburu is out with a hamstring tear. Albacete have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria (they host Celta Fortuna first), but José Corpas should still be suspended here (a three-match ban, per one report) and Higinio Marín went off injured at Leganés.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Burgos's last three home league games ended 2-1, 1-1 and 1-0, and Francisco has said he does not want an end-to-end game. Albacete win with few chances and could be without Higinio Marín.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners and I keep it. Burgos should have more of the ball at home, but Albacete under Etxeberria press high rather than sit deep, so the territory should not be completely one-way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, low for this division. I lean higher: Albacete's high press commits fouls, Burgos describe themselves as the hardest-running team in the league, and Corpas's recent red shows Albacete's edge. Five or six looks more likely than four.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. I lean lower: Albacete took only five shots against Sabadell and 12 at Leganés, and Burgos's controlled home games are not shot-heavy. The site's 10.3 for Albacete looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the shots and goals: Burgos's home wins have been narrow, and Albacete's goals have come from few efforts (both goals against Sabadell went in off opponents).
